propositions: A concurrent commit landing between verify and sign steps causes the ticket to close without a completion signature, making the suggested re-close remedy a no-op since the ticket is already closed

The verify_completion() call reads HEAD independently from the pre-sign drift guard, allowing HEAD to resolve to different commits (A during verify, B during sign), causing the sign to refuse but the close to proceed anyway
The default (no --ref) code path still reads HEAD twice and splits verification from signing, whereas the --ref path introduced in 80af correctly pins both to the same ref
There is no first-class non-force recovery mechanism to obtain a completion attestation for a closed-but-unsigned ticket without --force-close or manual manifest fabrication
The entire verify+sign+close unit should atomically bind to a single pinned revision so unrelated concurrent commits cannot split the verified state from the signed state
